text:
Olivia: ping — AcmePay is seeing a spike of 504s and intermittent 5xx from hosted inference. Customer says p95 latency jumped from ~120ms to 1.8s and then timeouts ~13:02 UTC. They reported it under support ticket #ACME-8473.
Olivia: quick summary pasted from customer: "Many requests are hanging in the gateway; some succeed after 2s but majority get 504. Happening across models gpt-open-2 and opt-small. Started after ~12:50 UTC."
Olivia: sample curl they sent (they hit our API endpoint, token masked):
```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-open-2","input":"hello"}'
```
Olivia: their trace shows requests queued at gateway and then 504. They pasted a gateway log with this repeated pattern: ```[13:02:12] enqueue request tenant=acmepay id=abcd1234 queue_depth=512 evicted=false
[13:02:14] dequeue failed id=abcd1234 timeout=2000ms route=hosted-gateway status=504```
Olivia: attaching their raw logs in case we need to correlate. Can SRE triage? :eyes:
Oncall-SRE-Bot: Alert fired: hosted.gateway.queue_depth > 400 for cluster hosted-us-east-1 at 13:01:40 UTC. p95 latency increased 14x. Runbook link: https://go/redwood/runbooks/queue-surge
Ana: looking. Early thought: continuous-batcher backlog + KV cache warmup causing long dequeue delays. Saw similar pattern in #3162278001.
Tariq: can you paste the gateway metrics around 12:45-13:10? I want enqueue/dequeue rates and batch latency distribution.
Olivia: metrics snapshot: enqueue_rate spiked to 5k rps, dequeue_rate stayed 800 rps, queue_depth peaked 560, kv_cache_miss_rate jumped from 2% to 46%.
Kevin: that gap looks like batching backlog — requests pile up waiting for batching window or kv lookups. If kv cache misses spike, batchers stall waiting on DB/HW.
Lucas: I see tenant isolation is off for AcmePay (shared pool). If their traffic pattern spiked they could starve other tenants and also get starved due to head-of-line in the shared queue.
Tariq: repro steps request: can someone capture a tracer for a failing request with headers x-request-id and route? Need stack trace where it blocks. Olivia, can you ask AcmePay to provide one failing request id?
Olivia: asked, they sent id=abcd1234 and a trace id trace-76b. Pasting the trace span list (trimmed): ```enqueue->wait-batcher->kv-lookup->batch-send->dequeue-timeout```
Ana: that matches KV miss causing extended wait inside batcher; once one request waits it holds batch open longer causing tail-latency. Also queue depth limit (512) triggers eviction behavior.
Kevin: immediate mitigation options: 1) temporarily increase gateway queue depth threshold to 1024 for hosted-us-east-1, 2) force fast-fail for requests with long prefix (reject rather than block), 3) enable tenant rate-limits for acmepay to smooth incoming bursts. Which one do we want now?
Olivia: customer asks for quick fix — they prefer no interruption but want reliability. Suggest #3 first then #1 as fallback.
Tariq: agree. I'll deploy a tenant rate-limit rule (burst=800rps, sustained=500rps) for acmepay and watch. Lucas, can you prepare the queue depth throttle change in case rate-limit doesn't bring dequeue/enqueue closer?
Lucas: prepping a change — I can flip the queue_depth soft limit to 1024 and adjust eviction policy to LIFO for user-facing requests to reduce tail latency. Will wait for green from Tariq.
Oncall-SRE-Bot: Action logged: tenant-rate-limit applied acmepay burst=800 sustained=500 at 13:07:20 UTC by Tariq.
Tariq: deployed rate-limit. Monitoring now.
Ana: while we monitor, let's gather more diagnostics: stack traces from batchers, kvstore latency graphs, and model runtime queue lengths. If kvstore latency >200ms we need to throttle batcher reads.
Olivia: AcmePay reports that after 13:08 UTC their error rate dropped 70% and p95 down to ~250ms but a few 504s remain. They asked for ETA on permanent fix.
Tariq: good — keep rate-limit for 30m and observe. If stable, we can keep it and work on longer-term: tenant isolation (dedicated pool) or smarter batching thresholds.
Kevin: medium-term fix proposals: - auto-shed by tenant during kv-cache warming - adaptive batch windows based on current queue depth - pre-warm KV cache for high-traffic tenants at model load time
Ana: add one immediate config change: reduce max_batch_wait from 15ms to 8ms for small models in hosted pool — reduces tail at cost of small throughput hit. Propose rolling this for small-models pool in us-east.
Lucas: I will stand by to flip queue_depth limit if we see a new spike. Also I'll open a follow-up PR to add tenant-aware batching.
Olivia: customer confirming: errors nearly gone after rate-limit, they want a postmortem. I'll coordinate.
Tariq: assign postmortem owners: Ana (root cause), Kevin (mitigation design), Lucas (infra follow-up). Olivia will own customer comms. I'll keep incident open for 3 hours to confirm stability.
Olivia: noted. I'll update ticket #ACME-8473 and set expectation for a writeup in 48h. :thumbsup:
Oncall-SRE-Bot: Incident state: acknowledged -> mitigated (rate-limit applied) at 13:15:02 UTC.
Ana: quick note for postmortem: root cause hypothesis = sudden burst + high kv_cache_miss rate causing batching windows to extend and backlog at gateway; queue depth hit eviction threshold causing 504s for long-tailed requests.
Kevin: adding to followup list: evaluate increasing default queue_depth, add per-tenant backlog alerts, and implement KV pre-warm for top tenants.
Lucas: saving logs and traces to /var/log/incidents/3612349999 for PM.
Olivia: thanks all, will close after 3h of stable metrics.
Tariq: good job team. :clap:
